transcript: Many people who live with constant anxiety, the kind with no clear reason, are not only suffering in the mind, they are suffering in the gut. When I meet someone who is deeply anxious or depressed, very often their digestion is also in chaos, gas, bloating, cramping, diarrhea, constipation, irritability. This is not a coincidence. The same messengers that shape your mood also guide the rhythm of your digestion. When the mind is unsettled, the gut loses its natural pace. This is one of the most overlooked truths in modern medicine. Many people believe they have endless food allergies, wheat, dairy, soy, corn, fruit, gluten. The list grows longer every year. Yes, true allergies exist, but most of the time this is not an allergy, because an allergy does not come and go. You are not allergic on Monday, fine on Wednesday, and allergic again on Saturday. When the gut is weak, people blame the last thing they ate. But they notice something confusing. The same food felt fine yesterday, and today it causes discomfort. This tells us something important. The problem is not the food, it is the movement of the gut. When digestion slows or becomes irregular, food sits too long or moves too fast, pressure builds, inflammation rises, and the mind begins to feel uneasy, restless, and heavy. When the gut's rhythm is restored, the body calms, and when the body calms, the mind follows. This gentle restoration is what we practice inside the 30-day healing journey. Each day offers a short, simple guidance to calm the nervous system, support digestion, and bring the body back into balance. If you feel cold to begin, you can find the 30-day healing journey in the link on my profile.
